subsystems.name: Piezoelectric nanostructure
subsystems.role: generates a piezoelectric potential when mechanically strained.
parts: ZnO nanowires or other piezoelectric nanomaterial

subsystems.name: Semiconductor junction
subsystems.role: converts the piezoelectric potential into a change in charge transport.
parts: metal electrode forming a Schottky contact

subsystems.name: Strain applicator
subsystems.role: delivers controlled mechanical deformation to the nanostructure.

subsystems.name: Signal conditioning
subsystems.role: reads the small current or voltage changes produced by strain.

subsystems.name: Power management
subsystems.role: supplies power, or harvests it from the piezoelectric effect itself.

subsystems.name: Packaging
subsystems.role: protects the nanoscale device from moisture and mechanical damage.

buildSteps.title: Grow piezoelectric nanowires
buildSteps.detail: A seed layer is deposited on a substrate, then ZnO nanowires are grown in a solution at moderate temperature (hydrothermal method) or by vapour deposition.

buildSteps.title: Pattern and align the nanowires
buildSteps.detail: Photolithography or transfer techniques place nanowires where devices are needed, sometimes aligning them horizontally.

buildSteps.title: Form electrical contacts
buildSteps.detail: Metal electrodes are deposited so one contact forms a Schottky barrier and the other an ohmic contact, creating the piezotronic junction.

buildSteps.title: Integrate onto a flexible substrate
buildSteps.detail: The device is transferred or built directly on a polymer film so it can bend with movement.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate the device
buildSteps.detail: A thin, flexible coating seals the nanostructures against humidity and wear.

buildSteps.title: Connect readout electronics
buildSteps.detail: Wires link the device to an amplifier and digitizer that measure current changes under strain.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and test
buildSteps.detail: Known mechanical forces are applied and the electrical response is recorded to map strain to signal.

prerequisites.why: consistent size, orientation and crystal quality are needed for reproducible device behaviour.
reliable Schottky and ohmic contacts are essential for the piezotronic effect to work.
models linking strain to barrier height and current are still being refined.
wearable and implantable uses need devices that survive repeated bending.
self-powered sensors produce tiny currents that must be measured without draining a battery.

pathway.milestone: laboratory demonstrations of strain sensors and piezoelectric nanogenerators
pathway.unlocks: proof that mechanical motion can both power and modulate a device.

pathway.milestone: wearable health monitors powered by body movement
self-powered wireless sensor nodes for industrial and environmental monitoring
pathway.unlocks: dense sensor networks where wiring or batteries are impractical.

pathway.milestone: implantable biomedical devices driven by heartbeat or breathing
pathway.unlocks: long-lived medical implants that never need recharging.
